title: INFWAD – Vue stickers
description: De belangrijkste onderwerpen van de Vue-stickers (Vue les 1 t/m 6), uit de uitleg, de quizvragen, de oefentaken en de woordenlijst. Vragen, antwoorden en uitleg zijn in het Engels.

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: Why do modern frameworks like Vue use **reactivity**?
questions.explanation: Reactivity connects data and page, like a spreadsheet: change a cell and every formula that uses it updates.

options.text: So the page updates by itself when the data changes
So you can skip writing HTML
So CSS only affects one component

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: Which parts can a `.vue` **Single File Component** contain?
questions.explanation: One file, three rooms: script is the brain, template is the body, style is the clothes.

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text:
What does this button show after 3 clicks?

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
let count = 0
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>
```
questions.explanation: `let count = 0` is a normal variable. Vue only tracks reactive values such as `ref()`.

options.text: Nothing changes: count is not reactive

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: In the **script** you write {{1}} to show a ref's value, in the **template** you write {{2}}.
questions.explanation: Script: count.value. Template: just count, because Vue unwraps refs in the template.

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: `:` is short for {{1}} and `@` is short for {{2}}.
questions.explanation: : = "this is JavaScript, not text" (v-bind). @ = "when this happens" (v-on).

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text:
When `count` is 0 you see "Start counting!" **and** "Negative". What's the fix? ```html

Start counting!

Positive

Negative

```
questions.explanation: Now there are two chains. The second `v-if` is false at 0, so its `v-else` shows. One chain shows exactly one message.

options.text: Change the second `v-if` to `v-else-if`, so the three form one chain

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: What's the difference between `v-if` and `v-show`?
questions.explanation: v-if = build it or tear it down. v-show = put a blanket over it (display: none).

options.text: `v-if` removes the element from the DOM, `v-show` only hides it with CSS

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text:
What's wrong with this list? ```html
  • {{ product.name }}
    • ```
questions.explanation: Without `:` the attribute is plain text, so every item gets the same key. Write `:key="product.id"`.

options.text: The key is the text "product.id", because the colon is missing
`product in products` should be `products in product`

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: How does data flow between components?
questions.explanation: One-way data flow: the parent owns the data, so changes are easy to follow.

options.text: Props go down to the child, events go up to the parent
Events go down, props go up
Children change the parent's data directly

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: How do you declare that a component can emit a `delete` event with a number?
questions.explanation: defineEmits declares which events a component can emit and what they carry.

questions.title: Vue 1 – Vue basics
questions.text: ProductCard emits `delete` with the id. How does the parent run `deleteProduct` when that happens?
questions.explanation: The parent listens with `@` plus the event name. The emitted id arrives as the function's argument.

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text: What does `v-model` do?
questions.explanation: Typing changes the variable, and changing the variable in code changes the input.

options.text: It keeps an input and a variable in sync in both directions
It sends the form to a server

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text:
Why does the price become a string here?

```html
<input v-model="price" type="number">
```
questions.explanation: v-model.number converts what's typed into a number.

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text: Why use `@submit.prevent` on a form?
questions.explanation: .prevent calls preventDefault() on the submit event, so your function can handle the form.

options.text: To stop the page from reloading

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text: When should you use `computed()` instead of a normal function?
questions.explanation: A computed only recalculates when what it uses changes. A function runs on every render but can take parameters.

options.text: For a value worked out from reactive data that you want cached
When you need to pass parameters
When you want it to run every time

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text:
The template crashes with "totalValue is not a function": ```html

Total Value: ${{ totalValue() }}

``` How do you fix it?
questions.explanation: A computed property is a value, not a function.

options.text: Write `{{ totalValue }}`: use a computed like a variable, without `()`

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text: What is a **composable**?
questions.explanation: It returns refs, computed values and functions that any component can use. A toolbox you can lend to any component.

options.text: A function, usually named `useSomething`, that holds reusable logic

questions.title: Vue 2 – Forms and reusable logic
questions.text: A component does `const { count, increment } = useCounter()`, but `increment` is undefined. What's the likely bug in `useCounter`?
questions.explanation: A composable only shares what it returns: `return { count, increment, decrement }`.

options.text: `increment` is not in the object it returns

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.text:
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted } from 'vue'
console.log('A')
onMounted(() => console.log('B'))
console.log('C')
</script>
```
In which order are the letters logged?
questions.explanation: Code in script setup runs right away when the component is created. onMounted runs later, once the HTML is on the page.

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.text: Where should you load data or touch the DOM?
questions.explanation: onMounted runs once the component is rendered. Before that, `document.querySelector('h1')` finds nothing.

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.explanation: That's a memory leak. Remove the listener in onUnmounted.

options.text: The keydown listener keeps running after the component is gone

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.text: localStorage: {{1}} saves, {{2}} loads. Before saving an array you use {{3}}, after loading you use {{4}}.
questions.explanation: setItem = save, getItem = load. Objects go through JSON first.

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.explanation: By default Vue only notices when you replace the whole array, not when you push into it or edit a product.

options.text: It needs `{ deep: true }` to notice changes inside the array

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.text: What does `{ immediate: true }` do on a watcher?
questions.explanation: Handy when a form must fill in from a prop that already has a value at the start.

options.text: It also runs the watcher once right away, not only after the first change
It makes the watcher run synchronously
It stops the watcher after one run

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle and watchers
questions.text: Which of these are **side effects** (a job for `watch`, not `computed`)?
questions.explanation: A side effect is an action besides returning a value. Deriving a value is a job for computed.

options.text: Working out the total price of all products
Counting how many products there are

questions.title: Vue 4 – Component communication
questions.text: What happens when a child component runs `props.price = 0`?
questions.explanation: Props are a library book: read it, don't write in it. Emit an event and let the parent change its own data.

options.text: Vue blocks it and shows a warning: props are read-only

questions.title: Vue 4 – Component communication
questions.text: A form component must not change its `editingProduct` prop. What does it do instead when the user saves?
questions.explanation: The child copies the values into its own refs and emits the result. The parent updates its own data.

options.text: Build a new product object from its own refs and emit it, like `emit('update', updated)`
Store it in a global variable

questions.title: Vue 4 – Component communication
questions.text: ProductCard emits `delete`. ProductList sits between ProductCard and the page. How does ProductList pass it up?
questions.explanation: Event re-emitting: ProductCard → ProductList → ProductManagementPage.

options.text: It doesn't need to: events bubble up automatically
It calls the page's function directly

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text: What does `<RouterView />` do?
questions.explanation: The router swaps whatever component matches the URL into RouterView.

options.text: It's the placeholder where the current page's component appears

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text:
Links do nothing. What's wrong with this `main.ts`?

```ts
const app = createApp(App)
app.mount('#app')
app.use(router)
```
questions.explanation: A plugin is registered on the app before mounting: createApp → app.use(router) → app.mount.

options.text: The router must be imported in App.vue instead

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text: Why use `RouterLink` instead of `<a>`?
questions.explanation: A full reload restarts your app and loses its state: the counter in App.vue goes back to 0.

options.text: `<a>` reloads the whole page; RouterLink swaps the page without reloading
RouterLink only works for external sites

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text: {{1}} tells you where you are (like `route.params.id`); {{2}} lets code take you somewhere (like `router.push('/products')`).
questions.explanation: useRoute() = where am I? useRouter() = take me somewhere.

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.explanation: "2" === 2 is false, so nothing matches.

options.text: Route params are strings, so compare with `Number(route.params.id)`
The route needs a `*` at the end

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text: What does the route `/:pathMatch(.*)*` do?
questions.explanation: Point it to a NotFoundPage so unknown URLs show a friendly 404. Without it, RouterView shows nothing.

options.text: It catches every URL that no other route matched
It matches only the home page

questions.title: Vue 5 – Routing
questions.text: What does `component: () => import('../pages/AboutPage.vue')` do?
questions.explanation: That's lazy loading: a dynamic import makes a separate .js file that's downloaded on demand.

options.text: It loads the About page only when someone visits it
It makes the page load first
It imports the page into every route

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: What are the three states of a Promise?
questions.explanation: Loading, error and success are the three **UI** states you show for async data.

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.explanation: Write `async function loadProducts() { … }`. async = this function is allowed to wait.

options.text: `await` only works inside a function marked `async`

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.explanation: response.json() reads the body and also returns a Promise.

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: What does `fetch()` do when the server answers 404?
questions.explanation: fetch only fails when there's no connection at all.

options.text: It succeeds; you have to check `response.ok` yourself

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: Why put `loading.value = false` in `finally`?
questions.explanation: At the end of try, a failed request would leave "Loading…" on screen forever.

options.text: `finally` runs whether the request worked or failed

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text:
When there is an error you see the error **and** the list. What's the fix? ```html
Loading products...
{{ error }}
```
questions.explanation: Loading, error and success: one v-if / v-else-if / v-else chain shows exactly one.

options.text: Put the error inside the list

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: The API calls the name `title`, your Product type calls it `name`. Where does the course say to fix that?
questions.explanation: Data transformation at the boundary: the rest of the app never sees the API's names.

options.text: Right where the data comes in: `data.map(item => ({ id: item.id, name: item.title, ... }))`
In every template that shows a product
By renaming your interface to use title
